topic: What if gravity doubled every hour?

script.text: In the water, you can breathe. Barely. Your mom, Ellie, Mr. Patel, Biscuit, all floating with just your faces out, staring at the sky.
The whole street is in that pool. Nobody talks. Breathing takes all you've got.
High above you, a plane you can barely see is still coming down, slow and careful, toward the highway. It makes it. Mr. Patel lets out a breath he's been holding for an hour.
Nine fifty-nine. Ellie squeezes your hand. Sixteen g is coming.
The water lifts out of the pool like a giant wobbling bubble. With all of you still inside it. Floating up. Past the roof. Past the trees.
And down the street, the whole ocean is starting to rise.

Is any of this real? The physics is. Your blood really does weigh more as gravity grows. Pilots really do black out at a few g. And water really does push back harder as gravity gets stronger. The sources are in the description.
But who flipped the switch at ten o'clock? Tell me your theory in the comments. Part two is coming.
